input.summary: Meridian's seven ownership domains are mapped; 97% are candidate-grade, blocking use-case accountability assignment.
covers: Org ownership mapping across seven functional domains
Executive sponsor alignment to five priority use cases
Active vs. candidate domain readiness status
Evidence confidence distribution across 228 ownership records
Accountability gaps blocking decision-grade use-case advancement
sources: Synthetic PHI-free planning-grade context — not real Meridian production data

story.meaning: Meridian has seven named ownership domains and seven executive sponsors, but 97% of org rows remain candidate-grade — accountability is declared, not yet decision-grade.
story.observed: Six of seven domains are active; Finance and Actuarial is candidate-only. All five priority use cases carry at least one unresolved evidence gate that no single owner has formally closed, leaving sponsorship diffuse across CEO, CFO, CIO, CDAO, and Chief Experience Officer.
story.matters: Without certified domain ownership, use-case accountability cannot be assigned. Every evidence gate — medallion architecture, data governance, transcript governance, contract digitization — requires a named owner with authority to close it. Diffuse sponsorship is the primary reason all five use cases remain in planning.
story.supports: Nexus org dimension provides the accountability spine. Closing candidate-to-active promotion for Finance and Actuarial, and assigning a single accountable executive per evidence gate, is the prerequisite action before any use case can advance to sourcing.

findings: 228 org ownership records mapped; only 6 are active — the remaining 222 candidate rows mean accountability is asserted but not yet certified across Meridian's domain structure.
Finance and Actuarial is the only domain flagged candidate-only despite CFO sponsorship of four priority use cases, creating a direct accountability gap for cost transparency and automated close.

All five CEO-priority use cases have multi-domain sponsors but no single accountable owner per evidence gate — diffuse sponsorship is the structural blocker preventing planning-to-decision advancement.
164 high-confidence and 64 medium-confidence records indicate strong signal quality; the bottleneck is governance formalization, not data availability.

org → evidence (domain owners must close evidence gates per use case)

org → data (domain ownership determines semantic layer stewardship)
relationships.note: Org ownership is the accountability spine for Meridian's entire use-case portfolio. Until candidate domains are promoted to active and single owners are assigned per evidence gate, risk, data, and use-case dimensions cannot reach decision grade — each dimension's gaps trace back to an unresolved org accountability.

evidence.name: Org Ownership CSV — Domain Anchor Records
evidence.facts: Seven functional domains identified; six active, one (Finance and Actuarial) candidate-only. Confidence: 164 high, 64 medium. 89% evidence coverage across 223 referenced records.
evidence.supports: Establishes the accountability spine for all five priority use cases and confirms domain-level readiness status
evidence.missing: Candidate-to-active promotion criteria not documented; no RACI or evidence-gate ownership fields present in source

evidence.name: Executive Intent Interviews — CEO / Enterprise Strategy
evidence.facts: CEO sponsors six use cases across all seven domains. All six flagged as promising but not decision-grade. Primary blockers: no certified medallion architecture, no formal data governance, no real-time integration proof.
evidence.supports: Confirms CEO as enterprise-level sponsor but highlights absence of single-owner accountability per evidence gate
evidence.missing: No formal CEO-signed RACI or evidence-gate closure authority documented

evidence.name: CFO / Finance & Value Intent Records
evidence.facts: CFO sponsors AI Benefits Realization Ledger, cost transparency, payment integrity, automated close, and AI spend governance. Finance and Actuarial domain is candidate-only — creating a direct accountability gap.
evidence.supports: Identifies Finance and Actuarial as the highest-priority domain requiring active promotion
evidence.missing: No CFO-signed domain activation, baseline, or benefits ledger tie evidenced

evidence.name: CIO / CTO / CISO Technology Domain Records
evidence.rows: 12 technology-domain records across CIO, CTO, CISO
evidence.facts: Technology Platform and Security is active/high confidence. CIO owns FY26 AI spend governance. CTO owns infrastructure and cloud. CISO owns AI governance/model risk. AWS/Databricks foundation is aspirational — not yet evidenced as production-ready.
evidence.supports: Confirms technology domain ownership but exposes gap between aspirational platform direction and certified foundation evidence
evidence.missing: No AWS/Databricks readiness gate owner formally assigned; no AI audit trail evidence loaded

evidence.name: Chief Experience Officer / Contact Center Domain Records
evidence.facts: Chief Experience Officer sponsors Member Service Agent Assist Transformation and Contact Center Platform/Knowledge Modernization. Contact Center and Member Experience domain is active/high. Transcript governance, real-time CRM integration, and member identity linkage are all unproven.
evidence.supports: Confirms CXO domain ownership; surfaces three unresolved evidence gates blocking call center optimization advancement
evidence.missing: AHT, FCR, transfer rate, CSAT, and QA baselines not loaded; transcript governance policy not evidenced
